A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, and all supplied text, tables, figures and equations are readable. v3 ends after its references; v4 adds Appendices A–F. The shared material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v3 reports original reading-recognition experiments, generalization tests, ablations and reading-type classification results in Sections 6.1–6.6.

after.justification: v4 retains these original results and adds baseline evaluations, detailed Columbus analyses and RGB-assisted reading-medium classification in its appendices.

M1.justification: The proposed modality encoders, transformer fusion, modality dropout and gaze augmentation remain unchanged in Section 4. The supplementary architectures are comparison methods, while the additional configurations test the existing method.

E1.justification: The experiments retain Seattle, Columbus and EGTEA coverage, including reading recognition, reading-type classification and cross-language evaluation. The supplementary breakdowns and mirror analyses examine conditions already represented in the original datasets.

E2.justification: Appendix E adds evaluated comparisons with Llama-3.2-11B-Vision-Instruct, two-stream I3D, a GRU, a 1D CNN and an MLP. v3 contains modality and model-size comparisons but lacks these alternative-method evaluations.

E3.justification: The supplement introduces baseline-specific training and input protocols, VLM prompting and input variants, and a 10-degree RGB configuration for medium classification. Table 9 additionally reports AUC and accuracy/F1 at 90% recall. The existing main-text protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds Columbus breakdowns by content and medium, multimodal cross-language augmentation analyses, controlled mirror comparisons and extensive failure cases. Appendices E–F add VLM input ablations and an RGB-assisted medium-classification comparison.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added tables and plots report point estimates; classification confidence thresholds do not constitute statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Shared main-text results are unchanged, but substantial additional results appear. Examples include mirror-set accuracy of 78.9% for gaze and 66.1% for RGB in Table 12, and Llama accuracy/F1 of 76.7%/65.6% on Columbus in Table 13. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements to retained scores.

T1.justification: The task formulation and model equations remain unchanged. The supplement introduces no new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about the dataset, complementary modalities, efficient recognition and reading understanding. The supplement supplies additional support without changing those core claims.

C2.justification: Appendices B, D and F substantially expand qualifications and interpretation: tradeoffs in verifying reading and comprehension, misleading RGB crops that undermine successful gaze predictions, and failures during slow reading. Appendix E also develops sensor and deployment tradeoffs across alternative approaches.

D1.justification: Appendices B–C add extensive collection instructions, annotation and segmentation procedures, metadata examples, recruitment details and quality controls. Appendix E documents baseline architectures, optimization and prompts. These are primarily new disclosures; v4 also removes the front-page dataset link while retaining the release promise.

R1.justification: v4 adds references for I3D/Kinetics, the Llama 3 model family and Min–Corso gaze-based activity recognition. Appendix E provides focused positioning against these alternatives and emphasizes sensor fusion with standard transformers; the original related-work discussion is otherwise retained.

P1.justification: The existing main narrative and section order are essentially unchanged. Editorial changes affect contact information, the publication footer and acknowledgement placement. Added material is organized into a separate supplement rather than extensively rewriting the original exposition.

P2.justification: v4 adds Tables 7–14 and Figures 9–34, including dataset distributions, annotation examples, diagnostic plots, case-study sequences and baseline comparisons. These substantially expand the visual presentation; the original scientific figures and tables are retained.

improvement.justification: Appendices B–E substantially improve the dataset's reproducibility and the assessment of the method through detailed collection/annotation documentation, alternative baselines and controlled failure analyses missing from v3. These gains outweigh the removed dataset link and localized inconsistencies, including conflicting Columbus counts and the self-contradictory Figure 27 discussion. The improvement comes from documentation and evaluative depth, not higher headline scores.
